06

SDKs designed by language experts

One spec, nine SDKs. Every generator carries the same ergonomic features, so consumers get the same experience regardless of language.

TypeScript Python Go Java C# Ruby PHP Swift Rust
Type system
Strongly typed
Discriminated unions, schema validation, and forward compatibility, so old clients keep working as your API evolves.
Networking
Auto-pagination
Iterate offset, cursor, URI, and path-based pages with one method. Server-sent events and WebSockets included.
Reliability
Retries with backoff
Automatic retries with exponential backoff and idempotency headers, so transient failures never surface.
Auth and security
OAuth token refresh
Token refresh and webhook signature verification handled in the client, not in the prompt.

“We used an alternative SDK generator, OpenAPI Generator, for years, and customers constantly complained. Since adopting Fern, customers have migrated rapidly to our new SDKs and have been blown away by the quality.”

— Gil Feig, CTO, Merge

Each SDK reads as if it were hand-written by an expert in the language
07

Just run fern generate

Fern generates and publishes client libraries, so you focus on building the API.

Step 01
Import your API spec
Start with OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, OpenRPC, gRPC, or the simpler Fern Definition format.
Step 02
Select languages
TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Ruby, C#, PHP, Swift, and Rust. Generate locally as many times as you want.
Step 03
Add custom code
Extend the generated client with utility functions and business logic. Your changes survive regeneration.
Step 04
Publish packages
Fern semantically versions and publishes to each registry. Detect the API change, open the PR, release.
Tested by default
Unit tests
Cover every method so bad signatures fail before merge.
Mock server tests
Replay requests against a mock server so retries stay honest.
Integration tests
Run the SDK against a live API so behavior matches production.
Every generated SDK ships with its own test suite
